messages:
maya: Ran a concurrency sweep against v2-llama-13b-quant on the perf harness. tokens/s looks fine until ~8 concurrent runners, then we get stripes where throughput drops to ~40% and p95 latency jumps 3x. cost/token also spikes. 😕
tony: Do you have the runner logs or the harness command? is this in CI or local?
maya: Local repro first. Command: ```./harness run --model v2-llama-13b-quant --load=concurrency_sweep --concurrency-start=1 --concurrency-step=1 --concurrency-end=20 --batching=auto --samples=200```
maya: Attached a short excerpt of stdout: ```2026-11-03T10:12:45Z INFO batch_allocator: alloc batch size=32 slots=8 wait=12ms
2026-11-03T10:12:46Z WARN kvcache: miss_ratio=0.41 prefix_hits=0.18
2026-11-03T10:12:46Z INFO runner: serve_tokens=12345 p95=48.2ms tokens/s=810```
alex: That batch_allocator wait=12ms stands out. we merged a small scheduling tweak last week that pads slot allocation to avoid tiny batches; maybe it's overbuffering under certain concurrency shapes.
ton y: Can you share metrics with Prometheus queries? curious about slot_pressure and scheduling latency.
maya: Query I pulled: ```sum(rate(runner_tokens_served_total[1m])) by (concurrency)``` shows the stripes; also `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runner_response_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,concurrency))` spikes match the drop windows.
sarah: CI job failed earlier today on the same model, linking in case it's related: `ci-bot: build/rl-eval-782 failed (runner-integration)`.
ci-bot: build/rl-eval-782 — failed after 35m: tests:runner_perf_check (p95>target). See logs: https://ci.internal/rl-eval-782
kevin: Another useful metric: `sum(runner_concurrency_slot_pressure{model="v2-llama-13b-quant"}) by (concurrency)` — when pressure > 0.6 we see the throughput collapse. Also check `runner_batch_duration_seconds` buckets for long tail.
maya: I can repro reliably on my laptop + small cloud instance. When concurrency goes from 8->9 a subset of workers go into a backpressure loop: slots enqueue large batches then wait on remote allocator, creating synchronized pauses (the "stripe").
ton y: Sounds like coordinated scheduling. maybe we should try disabling the padding tweak and re-run. alex, can you revert the change in a branch?
alex: I'll open a quick revert branch and run a targeted sweep. cc @sarah for CI follow-up.
sarah: Good. I'll re-run the CI integration suite with a shorter timeout to capture logs earlier.
kevin: Quick workaround: set `--batching=max_batch_ms=5` on the harness to reduce padding window; reduces stripe severity in my local test, but increases tiny-batch cost. tradeoff.
maya: Thanks. Assigning next steps: alex revert + local sweep (alex), CI run with logs (sarah), prometheus dashboard panel for slot_pressure + batch_duration (kevin), and I'll instrument a lightweight sampling hook in the runner to capture allocation timestamps (maya).
alex: branch created: `revert/slot-padding-2026-11-04` and kicked off tests. link: https://git.internal/r/revert/slot-padding-2026-11-04
ci-bot: build/rl-eval-783 queued (revert branch).
ton y: Great. If revert fixes it we'll consider a variant that is congestion-aware instead of fixed padding. :thumbsup:
maya: I'll post a short PR with repro steps and the harness flags so QA can try the workaround. thanks everyone ❤️
